title: deliberate.py refuses clerk ballots mechanically
description: LIVE-FIRE FINDING from D-001: the W-002 charter says clerks NO legisla, NO vota, NO tiene stake, and deliberate.py accepted a proposer, three sponsors and three ballots from clerks anyway. A charter constraint nobody enforces mechanically is prose. deliberate.py must load the roster, resolve each identity's office, and REFUSE sponsor/ballot/proposer roles for clerk seats with a distinct error naming the charter line. Regression test: replay D-001's exact inputs and assert refusal at the first clerk sponsor.

notes.note:
T-417 CONSTRUIDO. La restriccion de la carta W-002 (clerks: NO legisla, NO vota) es ahora
mecanica en deliberate.py, con dos reglas y una postura:

1. NOMBRES NO EMITIDOS NO ACTUAN: los votantes de D-001 (clerk-relator etc.) ni siquiera
   estaban en el roster; un nombre sin plaza no tiene legitimacion para proponer, patrocinar
   ni votar.
2. PLAZAS CLERK NO LEGISLAN: la regla lee los marcadores de la carta DECLARADA del colegiado
   (NO legisla / NO vota) en vez de un nombre de colegio codificado, asi que un colegio clerk
   futuro con otro nombre queda cubierto el dia que se declare, y un colegio que retire la
   restriccion de su carta deja de tratarse como clerk.
BOOTSTRAP: una raiz sin roster.json no tiene gate (misma postura sin dia de bandera que
warrant.py); todas las pruebas preexistentes corren en ese estado y siguen verdes.

Gate instalado en los cuatro puntos de entrada: propose (proposer), sponsor (--by), prior y
vote (--voter). El replay de D-001 muere en su PRIMERA entrada, el propose de clerk-relator,
antes de que exista dossier -- y la prueba lo fija.

EVIDENCIA: 8 pruebas nuevas en test_deliberate.py (12 en el archivo), incluidos dos controles
negativos (ciclo de vida completo con nombres emitidos no-clerk; raiz sin roster conserva
bootstrap) y la prueba de que el colegio es clerk POR SU CARTA y no por su nombre. Suite
completa: 765 passed, 4 skipped.

REJECTED: mechanism holds against D-001 replay and all four gated entry points, but a real,
undeclared, untested escape survives.

REPLAYED (own execution, not producer's log):
- pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py -q => 12 passed (matches claim).
- pytest .harness/tests -q => 765 passed, 4 skipped (matches claim).
- D-001's opening move replayed verbatim (propose --proposer clerk-relator --evidence PR-022
  --evidence PR-060 --evidence T-399 --evidence C-001 --task T-416 --alternatives
  adopt-split-consequence maintain-zero-consequence unconstrained-coupling) against a scratch
  COPY seeded with the real .harness/roster.json (live .harness/deliberations/ never touched,
  still only D-001.json before and after) => "refused: unissued name: 'clerk-relator' holds no
  seat in the roster", exit 1, no dossier file written in the copy.

4 attack vectors I invented that HELD (mechanism correct, no bypass):
1. Whitespace-padded clerk name " fed-relator " -> stripped, then correctly refused as clerk
   seat ("clerk seat: 'fed-relator' sits in colegiado 'fedatario' ... AgentCity constraint,
   W-002"), not bypassed.
2. Case-varied "Fed-Relator" / "FED-RELATOR" -> fail CLOSED as unissued name (exact dict-key
   lookup), no privilege gained by the case trick.
3. roster.json chmod 000 (unreadable) and roster.json replaced by a directory -> both fail
   CLOSED with the explicit "roster unreadable: refusing every assembly act rather than
   guessing" message.
4. Full non-clerk lifecycle (propose/sponsor/prior/schedule/vote/conclude) replayed against
   the real roster copy with registro-a/registro-b/revision-doctrina/revision-mecanismo -> ran
   clean end to end, Condorcet concluded ("Winner: adopt"); negative control intact.

ESCAPE FOUND (blocking): assembly_eligibility()'s charter lookup silently fails OPEN when a
name's declared colegiado is missing from roster.json's colegiados dict:

    charter = ((data.get("colegiados", {}) or {}).get(colegiado, {}) or {}).get("incentive", "")

defaults to "" instead of refusing, so the clerk markers never match and the seat is waved
through as if it had no charter at all. This is NOT the declared/tested rosterless-bootstrap
case (roster.json is present, valid JSON, readable, and the name is still listed under
"names") -- it is a narrower, more realistic corruption (one colegiados key missing/renamed)
that the "roster unreadable" fail-closed branch never catches, because both Path.exists() and
json.loads() succeed.

Minimal A/B repro (scratch harness-roots only; live .harness/deliberations/ untouched
throughout):

  python3 - <<'PY'
  import json, pathlib
  data = json.loads(pathlib.Path("/path/to/real/roster.json").read_text())
  del data["colegiados"]["fedatario"]     # names["fed-relator"]["colegiado"] still = "fedatario"
  pathlib.Path("<scratch_root>/roster.json").write_text(json.dumps(data))
  PY

  # CONTROL (colegiados intact, copy of real roster.json, no edits):
  python3 .harness/bin/deliberate.py propose --title control --evidence T-1 --task T-1 \
    --proposer registro-a --harness-root <control_root>
  python3 .harness/bin/deliberate.py sponsor D-001 --by fed-relator --harness-root <control_root>
  # => "refused: clerk seat: 'fed-relator' ... AgentCity constraint, W-002", exit 1

  # TREATMENT (colegiados["fedatario"] deleted, everything else identical):
  python3 .harness/bin/deliberate.py propose --title treat --evidence T-1 --task T-1 \
    --proposer registro-a --harness-root <treatment_root>
  python3 .harness/bin/deliberate.py sponsor D-001 --by fed-relator --harness-root <treatment_root>
  # => "sponsored D-001 by fed-relator (sponsors: 2/3, status=proposed)", exit 0

A live clerk sponsors a real dossier, zero refusal message, indistinguishable from a
legitimate action. Reproduced identically for propose (clerk proposer becomes the dossier's
first sponsor). Not covered by any of the 8 new tests in TheClerkConstraintIsMechanical.

Related findings, judged NOT independently blocking:
- roster.json as a BROKEN SYMLINK also silently reopens bootstrap mode (Path.exists() is
  False for a dangling symlink, same code branch as no-roster-at-all): proposing as the real
  clerk name fed-relator succeeds, exit 0. This is bounded by D-17 (same OS user, no secret
  boundary) and by roster.json being git-tracked (git ls-files shows .harness/roster.json), so
  it crosses no new privilege boundary beyond the already-declared/tested delete-roster.json
  bootstrap posture (test_NEGATIVE_CONTROL_a_rosterless_root_keeps_bootstrap_behavior).
  Flagging for documentation, not blocking.
- schedule --speakers accepts a clerk name (fed-relator) ungated and gives it a speaking slot,
  but never adds it to sponsors or final_ballots (no stake, no vote gained). cmd_schedule has
  no actor argument at all to gate, and the producer's note enumerates only
  propose/sponsor/prior/vote as the four gated entry points -- reads as a declared scope
  boundary (matches fed-relator's own persona: "corre la deliberacion en orden aleatorio"),
  not a silent miss. Flagged, not blocking.

BLOCKING ISSUE is the colegiados-lookup escape only: the charter resolution must fail CLOSED
(refuse, with a distinct message) when a name's declared colegiado is absent from the roster's
colegiados dict, consistent with the fail-closed posture already used for
unreadable/malformed roster.json in the same function, and needs a regression test.

Housekeeping: lock.py status showed 2 live (unexpired) locks held by main/T-420 on unrelated
files (.harness/bin/reputation.py, .harness/tests/test_reputation_phase_b.py); lock.py sweep
=> "swept 0 expired lock(s)".

Verifier REJECTED with a real escape: a name whose declared colegiado is missing from roster colegiados resolves charter to empty string and is waved through. Fix: fail closed on orphan colegiado, plus regression test replaying the verifier's A/B repro.

HANDOFF -> verifier: Round 2. The rejected escape is closed IN THE MECHANISM: assembly_eligibility no longer resolves a missing colegiado to charter='' -- an orphan colegiado (name's declared college absent from colegiados) now refuses with 'roster inconsistent', same fail-closed posture as an unreadable roster. Sibling hole closed in the same move: an existing colegiado with empty/absent incentive text also refuses ('no charter text'), because a charter that cannot be read cannot be checked for the clerk markers. Regression class AnInconsistentRosterFailsClosed subclasses TheClerkConstraintIsMechanical so the parent's 8 tests re-run against the same fixture as the A/B control; 4 new tests replay the verifier's exact repro (sponsor --by fed-relator with colegiados['fedatario'] deleted -> was exit 0, now exit 1 'roster inconsistent'), plus propose, prior and vote via the same hole, plus the empty-charter sibling. Evidence: pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py -q -> 24 passed; full suite 798 passed, 4 skipped. The two non-blocking findings from round 1 stand as declared scope: broken-symlink roster reopens bootstrap (bounded by D-17 + git-tracked roster; documented, not gated) and schedule --speakers remains ungated (relator persona runs the deliberation; no actor arg exists on cmd_schedule). Files: .harness/bin/deliberate.py (assembly_eligibility), .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py.

VERIFIED (round 2). Round-1 escape is closed in the mechanism; replayed the exact A/B repro
myself against a scratch copy of the real roster.json (live .harness/roster.json and
.harness/deliberations/ untouched throughout, confirmed via git status --short):

  CONTROL (intact roster): sponsor D-001 --by fed-relator -> "refused: clerk seat: 'fed-relator'
    sits in colegiado 'fedatario' ... AgentCity constraint, W-002", exit 1 (unchanged).
  TREATMENT (colegiados["fedatario"] deleted, names["fed-relator"] unchanged): sponsor D-001
    --by fed-relator -> "refused: roster inconsistent: 'fed-relator' declares colegiado
    'fedatario' which does not exist in the roster; refusing rather than resolving its charter
    to nothing", exit 1. Round-1 finding was exit 0 silent pass; now exit 1 refusal. CLOSED.

Producer's 5 claims, all replayed by me (own execution, not the log):
1. pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py -q -> 24 passed. Matches.
2. pytest .harness/tests -q -> 798 passed, 4 skipped. Matches.
3. Exact repro above: confirmed treatment refuses, control unchanged.
4. Sibling hole (empty incentive on an EXISTING, still-owned colegiado 'fedatario') -> own
   manual repro: "refused: roster inconsistent: colegiado 'fedatario' declares no charter text
   (incentive) ... refusing rather than guessing", exit 1. Confirmed.
5. Read AnInconsistentRosterFailsClosed in test_deliberate.py: subclasses
   TheClerkConstraintIsMechanical so the 8 parent tests re-run as the A/B control against the
   fixture; 4 new tests cover sponsor/propose/prior/vote via the orphan-colegiado hole plus the
   empty-charter sibling. Confirmed by reading the diff, not just running it.

Cognitive diversity: I did not just re-run the producer's sponsor repro. I drove propose and
vote directly against the same orphan-colegiado fixture (different entry points than the
producer's regression tests exercised in isolation) and both refused identically ("roster
inconsistent: 'fed-relator' declares colegiado 'fedatario' which does not exist"), confirming
the fix is applied at all four gates, not just sponsor. I also independently verified the
rosterless-bootstrap negative control with my own CLI invocation (no roster.json at all,
--proposer anybody-clerk-named) -> exit 0, dossier created, no flag day.

7 NEW attack vectors of my own (all scratch harness-roots, never the live roster/deliberations):
1. colegiados["fedatario"] = null (colegiado value null) -> "no charter text", exit 1. HELD.
2. names["fed-relator"] = null (names entry null) -> falls back to colegiado="", "does not
   exist in the roster", exit 1. HELD.
3. colegiados key deleted entirely from the roster dict -> same "does not exist", exit 1. HELD.
4. names["fed-relator"]["colegiado"] = "" (explicit empty string) -> "does not exist", exit 1.
   HELD.
5. names["fed-relator"]["colegiado"] key absent entirely -> same as #4 via the "" default,
   exit 1. HELD.
6. Whitespace-padded colegiado " fedatario " (key exists as "fedatario" without spaces) ->
   exact dict-key match fails, "does not exist", exit 1 (refuses, does not bypass). HELD.
7. Consistently-renamed college (colegiados key "fedatario"->"Fedatario", name's colegiado
   field updated to match) -> still correctly detected as clerk via charter text, exit 1.
   Confirms the charter-not-name design intent, not a bypass.

2 NEW findings, judged NOT blocking (documented, not gated):
- Forged colegiados[""] entry with a harmless charter, COMBINED with rewriting
  names["fed-relator"]["colegiado"] to "" -> passes eligibility silently (sponsor succeeds,
  exit 0). This requires simultaneously fabricating a new colegiados entry AND reassigning an
  existing name's college -- full roster forgery, not a single missing/renamed field like the
  round-1 class. It is bounded by the same declared-out-of-scope threat model round-1 already
  used for the broken-symlink finding: roster.json is git-tracked and every agent runs as the
  same OS user (D-17, no secret boundary) -- reassigning fed-relator to any college by editing
  roster.json directly is not a new privilege boundary crossed by assembly_eligibility().
- colegiados[colegiado] set to a non-dict (bare string or list) crashes with an unhandled
  Python AttributeError/traceback instead of a clean "roster inconsistent" message. This is
  NOT a silent bypass: refuse_ineligible() is called before `with hc.guarded()` opens, so
  nothing is written and the action still fails (exit 1) -- it fails closed, just ugly.
  Robustness/UX gap, not a security escape; no clerk or unissued name gains standing.

Both are flagged for documentation/backlog, same category as round 1's own two declared
non-blocking findings (which the producer's note correctly carried forward unchanged: broken
symlink bootstrap and ungated schedule --speakers). Neither crosses a new privilege boundary
and neither reopens the round-1 blocking escape.

Housekeeping: lock.py status -> "no active lock files"; lock.py sweep -> "swept 0 expired
lock(s)". No stale leases to report.

VERDICT: done. The round-1 blocking escape (orphan colegiado silently resolving to charter="")
is closed in the mechanism, verified by my own replay plus 7 additional attack vectors I
devised myself, at all four gated entry points, with the negative controls (non-clerk
lifecycle, rosterless bootstrap) confirmed intact.
